title: The Structural, Paragraph, and Sentence Passes

transcript: Welcome to Course 4: Proofreading & Academic Editing. In this lecture, we introduce the professional editing system used by top academic journals: the Three-Pass Editing Architecture.

Most postgraduate students edit linearly—starting on page 1 and correcting commas while simultaneously trying to rethink their theoretical claims. This approach produces cognitive overload and misses critical structural flaws.

The Three-Pass framework splits editing into three distinct, non-overlapping passes: Pass 1 is Structural—you evaluate overall thesis architecture, section transitions, and argumentative continuity without touching commas. Pass 2 is Paragraph Cohesion—you check that every paragraph opens with a clear topic sentence and flows logically. Pass 3 is Sentence Mechanics—you fix nominalizations, subject-verb agreements, and formatting.
By separating macro-architecture from micro-mechanics, you cut your editing time in half and produce a vastly more rigorous, defense-ready manuscript.
key: Never edit sentence mechanics and thesis structure in the same reading pass.
Pass 1 (Structural): Verify macro-argument flow, logical progression between chapters, and heading hierarchies.
Pass 2 (Paragraph): Inspect topic sentences, internal evidence synthesis, and concluding bridge sentences.
Pass 3 (Mechanics): Polish academic register, eliminate nominalizations, fix articles (a/an/the), and format citations.
